tb/cocotb/soc/axi4_slave_model.py: complete rewrite using edge-based handshake: (1) AW/W/AR: assert ready, poll RisingEdge+ReadOnly loop, await RisingEdge after break to deassert in active phase; (2) B/R: assert valid in active phase, poll ReadOnly+RisingEdge loop (check current ReadOnly first to match BFM pattern), await RisingEdge after break; (3) R multi-beat loop: mandatory await RisingEdge at TOP of each beat iteration to guarantee active-phase context before driving rid/rdata/rvalid/rlast
notes: Key lesson: in cocotb with Verilator, the canonical AXI4 handshake pattern for a READY responder is: assert ready (active), poll [await ReadOnly; if valid: break; else: await RisingEdge], then await RisingEdge before deassert. For a VALID initiator: assert valid+data (active), poll [await ReadOnly; if ready: break; else: await RisingEdge], await RisingEdge before deassert. The DECERR engine uses combinational awready (valid only during DW_IDLE, cleared at the same rising edge where aw_unmapped is captured), so the BFM must sample ReadOnly of the drive cycle, not just T+1. Multi-beat loops must start each beat with await RisingEdge to avoid executing signal writes while still in ReadOnly context from the previous beat's break.

issues_encountered: test_soc_coherency.py: all 3 tests timeout at GPU_POLL loop (last_pc=0x11a8) after 600k cycles — GPS_DONE never asserts

Root cause: axi4_crossbar.sv AR channel protocol violation — R_IDLE→R_AR is registered (1 cycle latency), but s_arvalid in R_AR is driven combinatorially from m_arvalid. GPU ifetch master (gpu_compute_unit) drops if_arvalid_o exactly 1 cycle after issuing (warp_busy set by warp_issue_o per AXI4 spec: master MUST hold arvalid until arready). Crossbar enters R_AR cycle N+1 with m_arvalid=0; presents s_arvalid=0 to SRAM; SRAM arready never fires; crossbar stuck in R_AR; GPU fetch_stall infinite.

Fix required in axi4_crossbar.sv: either (a) latch address+valid at R_IDLE→R_AR and hold s_arvalid=1 from register in R_AR state, or (b) combinatorial decode in R_IDLE: grant arready to master and forward to slave simultaneously, then register rsel for R_DATA routing. Option (b) is zero-latency and recommended.

Root cause (confirmed via internal FIFO pointer tracing against a known-zero baseline, AND via a controlled fix): the test's release write (dut.s_bready.value=1) fires asynchronously right after a trailing m_clk RisingEdge inside _poll_until, with no s_clk synchronisation. At a slow s_clk this lands only nanoseconds before the next s_clk edge while s_bvalid is already high. cocotb's RisingEdge+ReadOnly sampling of that edge ends up one edge out of phase with what cdc_gray_fifo's own always_ff used for its rd_en at that same edge, so the software _count_handshakes_bg counter (from bead 5ej's fix) permanently undercounts one real, already-delivered completion. Since the FIFO then genuinely drains (no further supply), the test's count==target completion gate can never be satisfied -- a SOFTWARE stall, not a DUT deadlock.

Directly disproved a DUT bug: (1) internal wr_bin_q/rd_bin_q pointer trace on u_b_fifo shows exactly 9 writes = 9 reads for a 9-write saturation workload, fully self-consistent, no overflow, no reset-value-advertises-availability signature (explicitly checked for -- the exact class that produced the two prior bugs 4398c2e/7a9f9d4 -- and not present here); (2) synchronising the release write to a clean s_clk RisingEdge makes the identical reversed-ratio workload pass immediately and exactly (b=9/9 r=13/13, no stall); (3) the SAME async/unsynchronised release methodology at the REALISTIC direction (s=4 fast, m=9 slow) does NOT stall, because the fast s_clk's rapid follow-up edges self-correct the same single miscount before the target is exhausted -- explaining why the artifact only ever showed up in the reversed (slow-s_clk) direction, without implicating the RTL's direction-handling.
